free_tier.stated: anonymous guest read of 9 root entries; no account and no payment

per_object_cap.stated: the upstream provider's cap; the instance publishes none

retention.stated: until the operator's account or tenant fails; no TTL and no notice

egress.terms: served through cloudflare; the reader pays nothing

tooling: the AList/OpenList REST surface (/api/fs/list, /api/fs/get, /api/fs/put) and the WebDAV endpoint at /dav; the rclone alist backend speaks the REST
chaining: a fetch substrate: point a cache and two mirrors at it, never a write tier A read-only corpus, so there is no multiplication. Useful as a fetch mirror and as the reference implementation of publishing guest credentials and putting Cloudflare in front, which is the transferable part

limits.value: no published rate; one operator and a CDN front absorb the read
PUT denied at the guest role

identity_cost.detail: no registration; /api/me returns a guest session

reliability_note: The reference reader. A 7.43 TiB book and comic corpus, Cloudflare-fronted, and a 36,747,196-byte PDF read back at 206 with cf-cache-status HIT. The upstream is a SharePoint tenant, which is why single files reach tens of GiB.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200, JSON carrying a code field, site_title 'OpenList'
anonymous POST /api/fs/list on / returned code 200 with 9 root entries; write:true, write_content_bypass:False, provider:unknown
the zero-byte oracle (PUT at an existing directory with Overwrite:false) returned code 403 with message 'permission denied' inside HTTP 200, so the write permission failed and nothing was written

seed_facts.quota_verbatim: No stated quota. One /doc/出版 subtree alone lists 4,058,674,141,521 bytes, about 4.06 TB, as a single directory, with further subtrees at 0.94 TB, 1.36 TB and 0.33 TB. The visible corpus is in the tens of terabytes
seed_facts.chaining_verbatim: A read-only corpus, so there is no multiplication. Useful as a fetch mirror and as the reference implementation of publishing guest credentials and putting Cloudflare in front, which is the transferable part
seed_facts.reliability_verbatim: Alive and the read path is solid. Occasional cold-mount 500s clear on retry because the OneDrive backend hiccups and the instance does not. Upload throughput on a single stream was 20.2 MiB/s and eight parallel ranged GETs reached 20.48 MiB/s aggregate, which is already line rate, so there is no concurrency curve to take advantage of. The sweep file wrote these as MB/s; the probe moved 8 x 4 MiB, so the unit is binary and this is the correction
seed_facts.tooling_verbatim: AList 3.x WebDAV at /dav/ with the published guest credential alist:alist, PROPFIND Depth 1 returning 207 with 9 root collections; rclone webdav with vendor other; the REST API is anonymous
seed_facts.binding_note_verbatim: The read path is the best in the population and it is Cloudflare-cached, so egress is nearly free. What binds is that nothing can be written, which makes it a mirror and not a store.
